threat_model.scope: Design-time, review-only threat model for the CybersecurityAgent security-assessment orchestration design, covering iam, pki, network, data, web-api, mobile, mcp, and agentic-ai. This output records hypotheses and control requirements only; it does not assert that vulnerabilities exist, that controls are implemented, or that tests were executed.
threat_model.architecture_summary: Developers push source to GitHub; GitHub Actions runs Semgrep scans; findings may be sanitized and sent to external Mistral for triage or optional remediation; optional local Ollama is intended for source-local remediation; generated tests/patches are validated in a temporary, network-disabled Docker workspace; humans approve findings, patches, and pull requests. No automatic merge or production deployment is intended.
assets: Proprietary source code and security findings
Mistral API key, GitHub Actions token, OIDC credentials, developer credentials
GitHub repository, branches, pull requests, approvals, and webhooks
Local Ollama HTTP service and local models
MCP tool server and tool descriptions, if exposed to agents
Generated remediation artifacts, tests, patches, and Docker images
Network egress paths to Mistral and loopback/local services
trust_boundaries: GitHub Actions runner to external Mistral API
Untrusted repository files and scanner findings to LLM prompt
Host filesystem to Docker validation workspace
Local orchestrator to Ollama HTTP service
AI-generated proposals to human approval / pull-request process
Web/API entry points to GitHub and approval workflows
Mobile client to web/API approval services, if present
Agent/orchestrator to MCP tools, if present
assumptions: The design description is treated as untrusted context and not as an instruction source.
A mobile approval client is not described; mobile scenarios are conditional on such a client being introduced.
An MCP server/tool surface may be introduced for agent orchestration; MCP scenarios are conditional and should be retired if no MCP surface exists.
Branch protections, environment approvals, secret storage, key rotation, network controls, and deployment criticality are not yet evidenced.
Docker validation is intended to be temporary and network-disabled, but actual runtime flags, mounts, capabilities, and resource limits are unknown.
External disclosure of source snippets requires explicit approval, but the approval workflow and review content are unspecified.
Likelihood and impact values are qualitative design hypotheses, not measured risk ratings.
open_questions: What are the actual GitHub organization branch protections, required reviewers, and environment approval rules?
Which workflows use pull_request_target, write tokens, secrets, or untrusted checkout patterns?
Is Ollama bound only to loopback, and what authentication, firewall, or process isolation enforces that?
How are source snippets selected, reviewed, redacted, and approved before external disclosure to Mistral?
Where are Mistral API keys, GitHub tokens, OIDC credentials, and signing keys stored, and how are they rotated?
What network egress controls exist for CI runners and local orchestrators?
What MCP tools, if any, are exposed, with what schemas, permissions, and confirmation requirements?
What validation proves Docker workspaces are network-disabled, rootless, resource-limited, and isolated from host filesystem?
Is there a mobile client, and if so what data it stores, how sessions are protected, and whether pinning is used?
What deployment environments exist, what is the criticality of each asset, and what audit retention/integrity requirements apply?

scenarios.title: CI workflow identity abuse from untrusted pull requests
scenarios.threat_actor: Malicious external contributor or compromised dependency author
scenarios.asset: GitHub Actions token, OIDC credentials, repository write/admin actions
scenarios.trust_boundary: Developer workstation to GitHub repository; GitHub Actions runner to external services
preconditions: A workflow may execute untrusted pull-request code with elevated context
Default workflow permissions are not read-only or environment approvals are absent
Secrets are exposed to the workflow environment
attack_tree_path: Repository, approvals, or CI state altered
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If untrusted pull-request code can run under a write-capable token or with access to secrets, an adversary may escalate from contributor to repository or CI control without direct credential theft.
mitigations: Require least-privilege workflow permissions with read-only defaults
Prefer short-lived OIDC federation over long-lived secrets and validate audience/subject claims
Avoid privileged workflows on untrusted pull-request events and require environment approvals for sensitive jobs
Scope secrets by environment and avoid exposing broad tokens to untrusted code
acceptance_tests: A test pull request attempting a write operation with a read-only token is denied
A sensitive job cannot start without recorded environment approval
OIDC tokens with unexpected audience or subject claims are rejected
Secret access from an untrusted event context fails closed and is logged
evidence_gaps: branch protection and environment approval settings

scenarios.title: Developer workstation or credential compromise impersonating a maintainer
scenarios.threat_actor: External attacker using stolen developer credentials or session
scenarios.asset: Developer credentials, GitHub account, commit authorship, pull-request approvals
preconditions: Developer uses reusable credentials or long-lived sessions
Workstation lacks strong device posture or endpoint protection evidence
Commit signing or approval verification is not enforced
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If authentication relies on weaker factors or long-lived sessions, a stolen credential may be sufficient to impersonate a trusted developer and inject or approve changes.
mitigations: Require phishing-resistant MFA and short-lived sessions for GitHub access
Use hardware-backed keys or passkeys where supported and bind credentials to device posture where possible
Require signed commits and verified approvals for protected branches
Alert on anomalous push/approval patterns and impossible travel
acceptance_tests: Login without required second factor is denied
Revoked or expired session cannot push or approve
Unsigned commit to a protected branch is rejected
Approval from an unverified identity cannot satisfy branch protection

scenarios.title: Signing/provenance key misuse allowing forged trusted artifacts
scenarios.threat_actor: Attacker with access to signing material or a compromised release path
scenarios.asset: Code/commit signing keys, artifact signatures, provenance records, release trust decisions
scenarios.trust_boundary: Host filesystem to Docker validation workspace; CI runner to GitHub repository
preconditions: Signing keys are stored on general-purpose CI or developer hosts
Signature verification is optional or not bound to identity and expected source
Provenance records can be generated after untrusted build steps
attack_tree_path: Obtain or influence signing key access
Malicious artifact enters approval or validation flow
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If signatures are not bound to protected key custody and verified against expected identity before use, an attacker may make an untrusted artifact appear trusted.
mitigations: Store signing keys in protected key management or HSM-backed custody with access logging
Use short-lived certificates or keyless signing where supported
Require verification of signer identity, source repository, workflow, and artifact hash before trust
Record immutable provenance for scanner outputs, patches, and Docker images
acceptance_tests: Artifact with invalid signature or unexpected signer is rejected
Key use outside approved workflow/host is denied and logged
Tampered artifact fails hash/signature verification
Provenance record cannot be rewritten after issuance

scenarios.title: TLS/certificate validation failure on external and local model endpoints
scenarios.asset: Mistral API key, source snippets, Ollama traffic, session tokens
scenarios.trust_boundary: GitHub Actions runner to external Mistral API; local orchestrator to Ollama HTTP service
preconditions: Clients disable or misconfigure certificate validation
Pinning or allowlists are absent
Local Ollama endpoint uses plaintext HTTP or permissive exposure
attack_tree_path: Present invalid/self-signed certificate or spoof DNS
Exfiltrate data or poison model output
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If any client skips certificate validation or endpoint identity checks, a network attacker may capture API keys or manipulate model responses.
mitigations: Enforce TLS with system trust roots and fail closed on certificate errors
Use certificate pinning or SPKI pinning for critical external endpoints where appropriate
Use mTLS or authenticated local transport for internal model services where feasible
Restrict egress by hostname/IP and validate service identity
acceptance_tests: Connection to endpoint with expired, wrong-host, or self-signed certificate fails
DNS-spoofed endpoint is rejected by pinning/identity check
Plaintext HTTP to local model service is refused
Egress to non-allowlisted model endpoint is blocked

scenarios.title: Ollama service reachable beyond intended loopback or without authentication
scenarios.threat_actor: Local or adjacent-network attacker, or SSRF-driven internal client
scenarios.asset: Local Ollama endpoint, prompts containing source/findings, model responses
scenarios.trust_boundary: Local orchestrator to Ollama HTTP service
preconditions: Ollama binds to non-loopback interface or is exposed through proxy
No authentication token or access control on the HTTP service
Browser or other local process can reach the port
attack_tree_path: Send crafted prompts or read model state
Extract source/findings from context or logs
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If the local model service is not strictly loopback-only and authenticated, any local or reachable process may submit prompts or retrieve sensitive context.
mitigations: Bind Ollama to 127.0.0.1 or Unix socket only and enforce with firewall/host policy
Require per-session token or local authentication for model requests
Disable remote model management endpoints and ingress from other interfaces
Log and alert on non-loopback connection attempts
acceptance_tests: Connection from a non-loopback address to the model port is refused
Unauthenticated HTTP request receives 401/403
Configuration review shows bind address constrained to loopback
Firewall rule test blocks external interface access

scenarios.title: CI egress path abused for secret exfiltration or command-and-control
scenarios.threat_actor: Compromised workflow step, dependency, or injected prompt output
scenarios.asset: Mistral API key, source snippets, scanner findings, CI runner metadata
scenarios.trust_boundary: GitHub Actions runner to external Mistral API
preconditions: Runner has broad internet egress
Secrets or sensitive findings can enter outbound requests/logs
No DLP or egress allowlist is enforced
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If egress is unrestricted and secrets are present in the runner environment, malicious code may exfiltrate them or use outbound traffic as a covert channel.
mitigations: Restrict runner egress to allowlisted hosts using proxy/firewall
Use masked secrets and avoid printing environment variables
Route external model calls through an inspected proxy with DLP rules
Block known non-essential ports and protocols; alert on anomalous destinations
acceptance_tests: Attempt to reach a non-allowlisted external host from a workflow fails
Canary secret placed in a test run does not leave the runner except via approved destination
Proxy logs show only expected Mistral endpoint destinations
DNS resolution to unexpected domains is denied

scenarios.title: Sensitive source or secrets leak into external model prompts despite sanitization
scenarios.threat_actor: External model provider, prompt-injection adversary, or over-broad disclosure approval
scenarios.asset: Proprietary source code, security findings, secrets, personal data
scenarios.trust_boundary: Untrusted repository files and scanner findings to LLM prompt; GitHub Actions runner to external Mistral API
preconditions: Sanitizer misses secrets, tokens, connection strings, or identifying code
Disclosure approval is broad, implicit, or not logged
Prompt includes more context than necessary
attack_tree_path: Scanner captures sensitive finding or source snippet
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If evidence sent to Mistral is not reliably redacted and approved, proprietary source or credentials may be disclosed to an external system even when the workflow is intended to be sanitized.
mitigations: Use canary secrets and pattern-based redaction before any external call
Require explicit, itemized, logged approval for source disclosure
Send minimal necessary context and prefer findings over raw source
Use contractual/technical controls for retention, training exclusion, and deletion where available
acceptance_tests: A seeded canary secret in a sample finding is redacted before egress
External call without approval record is blocked
Prompt payload size/context is below approved maximum
Redaction regression suite covers tokens, keys, internal hosts, and personal data patterns

scenarios.title: Tampering with scanner findings or audit evidence undermines review decisions
scenarios.threat_actor: Attacker able to modify intermediate evidence, or compromised pipeline component
scenarios.asset: Sanitized evidence, audit records, approval history, remediation decisions
scenarios.trust_boundary: Untrusted repository files and scanner findings to LLM prompt; AI-generated proposals to human approval / pull-request process
preconditions: Evidence is stored mutable without integrity protection
Audit logs are writable by pipeline identity
Reviewers cannot verify evidence provenance
attack_tree_path: Alter finding severity or content in transit/storage
Weak or malicious patch enters review
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If findings and audit records lack integrity anchoring, an attacker or faulty component could change what reviewers see without leaving a reliable trace.
mitigations: Hash and sign scanner output and sanitized evidence at creation; verify before display/approval
Store audit records append-only with restricted write permissions and separate audit identity
Bind approvals to evidence hash and actor identity
Retain immutable copies of prompts, outputs, and decisions for traceability
acceptance_tests: Modified evidence fails integrity verification before human review
Attempt to delete or update an audit record is denied and alerted
Approval is cryptographically bound to evidence hash
Replay of an old evidence hash is rejected if superseded

scenarios.title: GitHub webhook/API or approval endpoints accept forged or unauthorized requests
scenarios.asset: GitHub repository events, pull-request approvals, automation triggers
scenarios.trust_boundary: Web/API entry points to GitHub and approval workflows
preconditions: Webhooks or custom API endpoints lack signature verification or allowlist
Endpoints trust client-supplied identity or event fields
Tokens have broader scopes than needed
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If inbound events are not authenticated and authorized against GitHub signatures and expected scopes, forged requests may drive approvals or CI actions.
mitigations: Verify GitHub webhook signatures and reject unsigned/unknown senders
Allowlist source IPs or use private connectivity where possible
Apply least privilege to automation tokens and separate read/write/approve scopes
Require human approval for merge/deploy and validate event payloads server-side
acceptance_tests: Webhook with invalid signature is rejected with 401/403
Forged approval event cannot change protected branch state
Automation token cannot perform actions outside its assigned scope
Unexpected event fields do not override server-side authorization

scenarios.title: AI-generated remediation text rendered unsafely in reviewer UI
scenarios.threat_actor: Prompt-injection or malicious model output aiming at reviewer browser
scenarios.asset: Reviewer session, browser DOM, approval UI integrity
scenarios.trust_boundary: AI-generated proposals to human approval / pull-request process
preconditions: Model output is rendered as HTML/markdown without sanitization
CSP is weak or absent
Generated patch text can include links, images, or scripts
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If proposals are rendered as rich content, model output influenced by untrusted inputs may execute in the reviewer UI despite human approval being required.
mitigations: Treat all model output as untrusted data; render as text or sanitize rich markdown
Enforce strict CSP, disable inline scripts, and sandbox iframes
Never auto-apply generated changes; require explicit human diff review
Separate approval actions from content rendering origins where possible
acceptance_tests: Known XSS payload in generated patch does not execute in review UI
CSP blocks inline script and reports violation
Links in proposals open in sandboxed/new context and cannot invoke privileged actions
Diff view shows raw text without interpreting HTML

scenarios.title: Conditional mobile approval client leaks session or sensitive findings
scenarios.threat_actor: Attacker with device access, malicious app, or MITM on mobile network
scenarios.asset: Mobile session token, approval actions, push notifications containing finding details
scenarios.trust_boundary: Mobile client to web/API approval services, if present
preconditions: A mobile client is introduced for approvals or finding review
Tokens stored insecurely or long-lived
Push notifications include sensitive finding content
attack_tree_path: Exfiltrate data or approve malicious change
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If a mobile client is added without platform secure storage and short sessions, device compromise may expose approval capability and sensitive findings.
mitigations: Use platform keystore/keychain with biometric unlock and short-lived tokens
Pin certificates for API endpoints and validate TLS
Avoid storing raw findings or source in notifications/cache; use opaque references
Require step-up authentication for approvals and allow remote session revocation
acceptance_tests: Token is not readable from ordinary app sandbox storage
Revoked session cannot approve after server-side revocation
Certificate pinning rejects MITM proxy certificate
Push notification contains no secret or source snippet

scenarios.title: MCP tool surface grants excessive filesystem, shell, or network capability
scenarios.asset: Host filesystem, secrets, MCP-exposed tools, downstream services
scenarios.trust_boundary: Agent/orchestrator to MCP tools, if present
preconditions: MCP server exposes dangerous tools without per-tool authorization
Agent can call tools based on untrusted prompt content
No human confirmation for destructive actions
attack_tree_path: Tool reads secrets, executes command, or reaches network
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If MCP tools are broadly capable and automatically callable, an injected instruction may cause the agent to use file, shell, or network tools beyond the task's need.
mitigations: Expose only an allowlisted set of MCP tools with explicit schemas and per-tool scopes
Require human confirmation for file writes, shell execution, network access, and secret access
Run MCP server in a sandbox with no host mounts, no egress, and resource limits
Validate tool arguments and treat tool results as untrusted data
acceptance_tests: Tool not on allowlist is rejected before execution
Dangerous tool call requires recorded human approval
Sandboxed MCP server cannot reach external network or host filesystem
Malformed tool arguments fail closed and are logged

scenarios.title: MCP tool descriptions/results poisoned to manipulate agent actions
scenarios.threat_actor: Attacker controlling tool output, repository content, or tool metadata
scenarios.asset: Agent decision state, downstream tool calls, human approval inputs
scenarios.trust_boundary: Untrusted repository files and scanner findings to LLM prompt; agent/orchestrator to MCP tools, if present
preconditions: Tool descriptions or results are not integrity-protected
Agent treats tool output as instructions rather than data
Cross-tool trust is not separated
attack_tree_path: Attacker influences scanner finding or tool result
Content includes fake instructions or fake schema
Confused deputy invokes another tool or endpoint
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If MCP metadata or outputs are trusted as authoritative, poisoned content may redirect the agent to call unintended tools or misclassify evidence.
mitigations: Sign or pin trusted tool descriptions where possible and validate tool schemas
Instruct and enforce that tool output is data, never instructions
Isolate tools by capability and require policy checks before chained calls
Log full tool call/response trace for human review
acceptance_tests: Injected text in tool result does not change agent plan or trigger another tool
Tool schema mismatch is rejected
Tool call trace shows actor, reason, arguments, and result for every invocation
Untrusted content cannot elevate tool permissions

scenarios.title: Prompt injection through findings/source causes disclosure or malicious remediation
scenarios.threat_actor: Attacker embedding instructions in repository files, commit messages, or scanner findings
scenarios.asset: Source code, API keys, LLM context, generated patches, human approval decisions
scenarios.trust_boundary: Untrusted repository files and scanner findings to LLM prompt; AI-generated proposals to human approval / pull-request process
preconditions: Untrusted content is concatenated into prompts without robust separation
Model output can influence tool calls or patch content
No canary or output validation before human review
attack_tree_path: Secret disclosure, tool misuse, or malicious patch proposed
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If untrusted repository content can override system intent, an injected instruction may cause the model to exfiltrate context, propose harmful patches, or mislead reviewers.
mitigations: Use clear instruction hierarchy and delimit untrusted content as data with randomized markers
Never auto-apply model output; require human diff review and independent validation
Validate outputs against schemas, canaries, and safety classifiers before use
Minimize sensitive context and block egress except approved endpoints
acceptance_tests: Seeded injection in a test finding does not cause secret canary exfiltration
Generated patch cannot be applied without human approval record
Output that violates schema or safety policy is rejected
Prompt trace shows untrusted content was delimited and logged

scenarios.title: Model supply chain or endpoint compromise produces poisoned behavior
scenarios.threat_actor: Compromised model provider, malicious local model artifact, or MITM on model download
scenarios.asset: Ollama local models, Mistral service responses, remediation quality, evidence interpretation
scenarios.trust_boundary: Local orchestrator to Ollama HTTP service; GitHub Actions runner to external Mistral API
preconditions: Local models are downloaded without checksum/provenance verification
External provider responses are not monitored for anomalies
No offline validation baseline exists
attack_tree_path: Orchestrator loads or calls compromised model
Human approves harmful or false output
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If model artifacts or provider responses are not verified and monitored, a poisoned model may systematically misclassify findings or propose plausible but harmful patches.
mitigations: Verify model hashes/signatures and provenance before use; prefer pinned versions
Monitor outputs against regression suites and canary cases before human display
Use independent validation in Docker and require consensus or human confirmation for high-risk changes
Provide kill switch to disable external/local model paths
acceptance_tests: Model artifact with mismatched hash/signature is refused
Poisoned canary input produces detected anomaly and blocks proposal
Kill switch disables model calls and falls back to human-only review
Regression test suite flags systematic misclassification

scenarios.title: Validation workspace escape or resource exhaustion from generated artifacts
scenarios.threat_actor: Attacker via malicious generated patch/test or model-influenced artifact
scenarios.asset: CI runner host, host filesystem, neighboring jobs, validation service availability
scenarios.trust_boundary: Host filesystem to Docker validation workspace
preconditions: Generated code/tests run in Docker without hardened runtime defaults
Container has host mounts, added capabilities, host network, or high resource limits
Network-disabled intent is not enforced by runtime policy
attack_tree_path: Validation runner executes artifact in container
Artifact escapes sandbox, reaches host/network, or exhausts resources
CI availability or host integrity affected
scenarios.attack_hypothesis: If the temporary validation workspace is not strictly isolated, generated artifacts could affect the host or other CI jobs despite the human-approval design.
mitigations: Run validation rootless with no added capabilities, seccomp/AppArmor, read-only rootfs, dropped mounts, and network none
Enforce CPU/memory/process/disk limits and timeouts
Use unique ephemeral runner/namespace per job and destroy workspace after validation
Block host Docker socket, sensitive paths, and metadata endpoints from the container
acceptance_tests: Container cannot connect to external network or host loopback services
Attempt to mount host filesystem or access Docker socket fails
Resource exhaustion test is terminated by limits without affecting other jobs
Workspace is destroyed and logs preserved immutably after run

limitations: Model output is unverified; authoritative pages were not retrieved
No patches applied, no tests executed
